report:
**Conclusion: No — the best available evidence indicates ivermectin does not lower the risk of death from COVID-19, and major health bodies recommend against its use for COVID-19 outside clinical trials.**

Early small trials and some meta-analyses suggested large mortality benefits, but several influential positive studies were retracted or found to be biased or fraudulent. When analyses are restricted to rigorous trials, the apparent benefit disappears. The large, double-blind TOGETHER platform trial (NEJM, 2022) found early ivermectin treatment did not reduce hospitalization or prolonged emergency care in outpatients, with no meaningful mortality effect. A Cochrane systematic review concluded the evidence was insufficient and of low certainty, finding no reliable mortality benefit. A 2022 critical appraisal of RCTs similarly found no convincing effect on clinical outcomes once study quality was considered. Reflecting this, the WHO updated its guidelines in November 2023 to strongly recommend against ivermectin for COVID-19, citing lack of evidence and biological plausibility; the NIH and FDA likewise advise against it.

In short, claims that ivermectin reduces COVID-19 deaths rest on low-quality or discredited studies; high-quality randomized trials and guideline bodies find no mortality benefit.
